title: Equivariant Borsuk-Ulam for Non-Prime Groups
description: Abstract framework for equivariant Borsuk-Ulam dimensions of cyclic groups Z/n with non-prime n. Derives lower bounds for Z/4, Z/6, and Z/pq from prime subgroup monotonicity. States the open conjecture that the BU dimension equals the maximum over prime divisors.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: buDim function, classical BU (Z/2), Yang-Borsuk (Z/p prime), monotonicity, open conjecture for composite groups.
originalContributions: Abstract buDim framework for cyclic group BU dimensions
Proved z4_lower_bound: buDim(4, n+1) ≥ n from Z/2 subgroup
Proved z6_lower_bound_z2 and z6_lower_bound_z3: dual prime bounds for Z/6
Proved zpq_lower_bound: general Z/pq bound from prime subgroups
Proved buDim_composite_has_prime_bound: every composite group has a prime-derived lower bound
Stated open conjecture: buDim equals max over prime factor bounds

sections.title: Abstract BU Dimension Framework
sections.summary: Defines buDim(n, d) as the equivariant Borsuk-Ulam dimension for Z/n acting on a d-dimensional representation.
sections.mathContext: The equivariant BU dimension measures how large a sphere must be before Z/n-equivariant maps to a d-dimensional space must vanish.

sections.title: Axiomatized Known Results
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the classical BU theorem (Z/2), Yang-Borsuk (Z/p prime), monotonicity under divisibility, and the trivial group case.
sections.mathContext: These are well-established results in equivariant topology. The monotonicity axiom captures the restriction principle: G-equivariance implies H-equivariance for H ≤ G.

sections.title: Bounds for Non-Prime Groups
sections.summary: Derives concrete lower bounds for Z/4, Z/6, and Z/pq from the prime subgroup monotonicity axiom. All proofs are fully machine-checked.
sections.mathContext: For Z/6 ≅ Z/2 × Z/3: both Z/2 and Z/3 embed, giving buDim(6, 2n) ≥ max(n, 2n-1) = 2n-1. The general Z/pq case follows similarly.

sections.title: The Open Question
sections.summary: States the central open question: does buDim(n, d) always equal the maximum over prime factor bounds? Formulates this as an axiom using Nat.primeFactors.
sections.mathContext: If true, composite group structure adds no extra topological obstruction beyond what prime subgroups provide. The resolution requires Fadell-Husseini index theory and representation-theoretic analysis.

overview.historicalContext: The Borsuk-Ulam theorem (1933) is a cornerstone of combinatorial topology. Its equivariant generalization replaces the Z/2 antipodal action with general group actions. For prime-order cyclic groups, Yang (1954) and Borsuk gave the definitive answer. The composite case remains largely open.
overview.problemStatement: For non-prime |G|, what is the optimal equivariant Borsuk-Ulam dimension?
overview.text: An abstract framework for studying equivariant Borsuk-Ulam dimensions of cyclic groups Z/n with composite n. The file axiomatizes the known results (classical BU for Z/2, Yang-Borsuk for Z/p, monotonicity under divisibility) and derives concrete lower bounds for Z/4, Z/6, and general Z/pq. All 6 theorems are fully proved from the axioms with 0 sorries.
overview.proofStrategy: Axiomatize the BU dimension function and known results. Derive composite group bounds from prime subgroup monotonicity. State the open conjecture.
keyInsights: Monotonicity under divisibility is the key structural principle for bounding composite BU dimensions
Both prime subgroups of Z/6 give the same bound 2n-1, so no additional information from having two primes
The open question reduces to whether composite groups have strictly higher BU dimensions than all prime subgroups

conclusion.summary: Abstract BU dimension framework for composite cyclic groups. 6 theorems proved, 6 axioms (5 known results + 1 open conjecture). Key result: all composite BU dimensions are bounded below by prime factor bounds.
conclusion.implications: The framework provides a clean algebraic setting for studying the equivariant BU problem without topological infrastructure. The open conjecture, if true, would show that composite group structure adds no extra topological obstruction.
openQuestions: Is buDim(n, d) = max_{p|n} buDim(p, d) for all composite n?
Are there exotic representations where composite groups give strictly higher BU dimensions?
What happens for non-cyclic groups (dihedral, symmetric)?
Can the Fadell-Husseini index be formalized in Lean to resolve specific cases?

crossReferences.description: Extends the classical Borsuk-Ulam theorem to composite group actions
